title: One global semantic commit, PR body and squash-merge convention enforced in every repository
body: Source: operator 2026-11-18 (verbatim): "ogólnie musimy też jakoś zrobić globalną zasadą semantic commits, do prów też chciałbym mieć taki znormalizowany sposób na opisy i mergowanie itp itd", with a screenshot of pingdotgg/t3code main: every squash subject reads `type(scope): observable outcome (#PR)`, e.g. `fix(web): a ~\ home path opens as a read-only home file, not as a project file (#38510)`.

Outcome: one global convention, rendered from KRN into the user-scope standards and enforced in every repository an agent works in, not only KRN:
1. Subject: `type(scope): outcome` where outcome states the observable behaviour after the change (what now works or no longer breaks), lowercase start, no trailing period, at most 72 characters; KRN keeps its `(t-id)` suffix; GitHub appends `(#N)` on squash.
2. PR title equals the intended squash subject; PR body has fixed sections (Why, What changed, Verified with command: verdict, Ticket/Refs when a tracker exists) produced by `krn pr body`, which also works in a repository with no KRN tracker.
3. Merge: squash only, squash title = PR_TITLE, squash body = PR_BODY, delete branch on merge, auto-merge on the required check; a `krn` command reports and (with --apply) sets these repository settings via gh.
4. Enforcement for agent work in any repository: a user-scope hook refuses `git commit` and `gh pr create`/`gh pr edit` whose subject or title breaks the format, with a message showing the expected form; it never blocks the operator's own terminal commits.

Proof: tests: the hook refuses `git commit -m "Update stuff"` and passes `fix(web): a cached page no longer shows stale prices`; krn pr body outside a tracker repo prints the sections; the settings command reports a merge-commit-enabled fixture as non-conforming; KRN itself is switched to squash body PR_BODY.
